overview: Black replies to 1.Nf3 with the pawn lunge 1...g5, offering the pawn to 2.Nxg5. Black hopes to build quick development with ...Bg7, ...d6 and ...e5, using the long diagonal against b2. White can take the pawn and return it when needed, getting a comfortable edge. This is a surprise try rather than a respected line.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with Nxg5 and consolidate with d4, e4 or g3
Fianchetto and punish Black's loosened kingside
Return material if needed to complete development

black_ideas.idea: Play ...Bg7 and ...e5 to open the long diagonal against b2
Strike in the centre with ...d5 and ...e5
Develop fast and use the g-file against the white knight

typical_structures.structure: White extra pawn with an open g-file for Black
Black pawns on e5 and d5 against a White fianchetto

character.notes: Early pawn offer and open lines lead to forcing, unbalanced play.

gambit.notes: Black gives the g-pawn for time and the long diagonal.

soundness.notes: White keeps the pawn with a good position, and strong players regard 1...g5 as unsound.

structure.notes: Black aims for central pawn breaks and diagonals, but the position is not fixed.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever play 1...g5; it is a surprise tactic.

level.notes: Few moves to learn, but it is dubious so never a beginner choice.
